detail.abstract: This paper explores the complex intersection between domain name Cyber-squatting and the right of publicity, focusing on cases involving celebrities and the Indian legal framework. Prominent examples include Donald Trump, Julia Roberts, and Mark Zuckerberg, who have faced cyber-squatters in India. These disputes are typically resolved through INDRP and WIPO's UDRP rules, but they also raise concerns about the right of publicity, a protection of an individual's marketable image or persona. The paper critically examines whether the right of publicity, traditionally seen as an economic right, can be equated to a fundamental right, as suggested by Justice Kaul in the Supreme Court's Puttaswamy decision. It argues that this alignment could create challenges, particularly since fundamental rights are in-rem and non-arbitrable, whereas economic rights are typically arbitrable. 1 By analyzing primary rules, case law, and scholarly works, the paper proposes a methodology for how arbitral tribunals can address right of publicity claims while considering their potential conflict with fundamental rights. 2 This discussion is crucial in understanding the evolving nature of personality rights in the digital age and the appropriate legal mechanisms for resolving related disputes.

title: The Stale Will: Event-driven review as a testamentary discipline — how a valid will goes wrong without being touched, and why the family may read a document the testator never wrote

detail.title: The Stale Will: Event-driven review as a testamentary discipline — how a valid will goes wrong without being touched, and why the family may read a document the testator never wrote

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of Valoren, a household continuity and personal-governance platform being developed through Standard Index Group. This working paper is an independent analysis of the mechanisms by which wills in England and Wales cease to reflect their makers' intentions, and of the review discipline that follows. No product, service, or commercial claim is evaluated in the paper, and the analysis is presented in method-neutral terms; the discipline described in § 6 is satisfiable without any commercial service. All views are the author's own.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a doctrinal legal analysis involving no human participants, personal data, or empirical fieldwork.
declarations.funderStatement: The author has received no external research funding for this work.

detail.abstract:
A will is executed once and read once, and the two moments are usually years apart. Everything in this paper happens in between. A validly executed will is not a system that tracks its maker's life; it is a snapshot of one afternoon of it. English law then operates on the snapshot mechanically as events occur. Marriage revokes the whole instrument (Wills Act 1837, s.18). Divorce does something stranger: the will survives, but every gift to and appointment of the former spouse takes effect as if that spouse had died on the day the marriage ended (s.18A). The sale of a specifically gifted asset deletes the gift, with no compensation from the proceeds (ademption). The death of a beneficiary before the testator deletes another gift by lapse, subject to a statutory rescue that reaches only the testator's own descendants (s.33). None of these mechanisms asks what the testator would have wanted. Each executes a rule, and the leading cases are a catalogue of outcomes nobody in the story intended — including one in which the testator's chosen charity lost its gift because his former wife had failed to die, and the estate went on intestacy instead.

The paper states each mechanism precisely, maps the eleven household continuity events of the companion taxonomy (SIG-WP-2026-02) to their testamentary consequences, and examines the mechanism by which "I have a will" — a true sentence — quietly terminates the attention the instrument still needs. It then sets out the discipline that follows: a short trigger list, a periodic floor, and a defined inspection, satisfiable with a diary and an ordinary solicitor's appointment. The reform context sharpens the argument. The Law Commission's 2025 recommendation to abolish revocation by marriage would, if enacted, remove the one mechanism that at least fails towards the formal spouse or civil partner and, where there are issue, the issue — and leave the pre-marriage will standing. The draft Bill contains a power to save a badly executed will. It contains nothing to save a perfectly executed one that has outlived its facts.

It has been difficult to estimate informal remittance flows yet important for central banks and policy makers to have an understanding of the volume, channels and usage of informal remittances,  including from the perspective of policy making and financial inclusion.  This Policy tool sets out a  survey and questionnaire approach developed for the use of central banks and statisticians for the purposes of collecting  data on informal remittance flows. It was created after indepth consultation with central banks in Asia, the Middle East and North Africa and Latin America.

title: Central Bank Activity, The Goodwin Pattern, and Secular Decline in the Wage Share
affiliations: New School for Social Research and

detail.title: Central Bank Activity, The Goodwin Pattern, and Secular Decline in the Wage Share
detail.abstract: In this paper, we present an alternative to the conventional view regarding the Goodwin pattern. We demonstrate that the Goodwin pattern emerges from a three-dimensional system of real, monetary, and distributional dynamics where the monetary linkage includes a central bank incorporating an asymmetric reaction function. The asymmetric reaction function is the result of a central bank that is inflation averse resulting in a deflationary bias. Therefore, the central bank sets interest rates in response to variations in the wage share and real activity, however, there is no influence of distribution on real activity. In our model, the central bank reaction function reflects implicit inflation targeting in real activity × wage share space responding to goods market and labour market pressure. In other words, the central bank finds itself in a conflicting claims environment, changing interest rates when either output or the wage share deviate from their target values. Our results show that the introduction of the central bank reaction function with a deflationary bias produces the cyclical behavior associated with the Goodwin pattern, but more importantly, it also demonstrates a weakening of the profit squeeze mechanism and a secular decline in the wage share.

title: Reaching for Duration
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco and

detail.title: Reaching for Duration
detail.abstract: Using historical data on U.S. commercial bank balance sheets, we show that banks' maturity mismatch has more than tripled since the mid-1980s, moving in close lockstep with declining interest rates and term premia. We rationalize these trends in a model of bank portfolio choice in which banks must cover operating costs out of current earnings. When term premia or short-term rates decline, banks extend the duration of their assets to remain profitable. This "reaching for duration" effect is convex in the degree of term premium compression. The resulting maturity mismatch renders banks increasingly vulnerable to self-fulfilling runs by uninsured depositors. Consistent with the model, less profitable banks subsequently raise their asset maturities, particularly in periods of low term premia and large Federal Reserve asset holdings. Quantitative easing, designed to remove duration risk from the private sector, may thus paradoxically concentrate it on bank balance sheets and undermine financial stability.

detail.abstract: The entrenched DIME framework and its expanded variants conceptually fracture American statecraft by treating national power as isolated, bureaucratic cylinders rather than integrated capabilities. To restore strategic depth, the U.S. national security apparatus must discard this additive mindset and adopt the 1918-derived "PPCE" (Political, Psychologic, Combat, and Economic) framework, which demands the simultaneous, inextricable admixture of these elements. Ultimately, realizing this capability-driven framework requires relentless executive enforcement and a transformation of institutional culture to prevent bureaucracies from defaulting to comfortable, lane-protecting silos.

title: Carbon Policy, Fiscal Sustainability, and Economic Growth in Nigeria: Assessing the Post-Subsidy Fiscal Transition
affiliations: Nuhu Bamalli Polytechnic, Ahmadu Bello University and Kaduna Polytechnic

detail.title: Carbon Policy, Fiscal Sustainability, and Economic Growth in Nigeria: Assessing the Post-Subsidy Fiscal Transition
detail.abstract: Nigeria's 2023 removal of its longstanding fuel subsidy constitutes one of the most consequential fiscal and carbon policy events in the country's post-independence history. This study reframes the reform as an implicit carbon pricing intervention and empirically examines its consequences for fiscal sustainability and economic growth over the period 1990-2023. Employing the Engle-Granger two-step cointegration approach, an Error Correction Model (ECM), and the Toda-Yamamoto Granger non-causality procedure, the study finds robust cointegration among the fiscal and growth variables across all three model specifications. The ECM speed-of-adjustment coefficient (-0.6424, p = 0.003) confirms that approximately 64.24% of deviations from long-run fiscal equilibrium are corrected annually, indicating a self-correcting fiscal mechanism absent in the pre-reform period. Government expenditure Granger-causes government revenue (χ² = 18.10, p < 0.001), confirming the spend-and-tax hypothesis, while government revenue Granger-causes economic growth (χ² = 5.68, p = 0.017). Gross fixed capital formation Granger-causes government revenue (χ² = 4.92, p = 0.027), establishing an investment-revenue-growth causal chain. These findings carry direct implications for Nigeria's National Determined Contribution (NDC) commitments and green fiscal policy design in resource-dependent economies.

title: Capital Flows and the Global Collateral Cycle
affiliations: Yale University, University of Virginia and Williams College

detail.title: Capital Flows and the Global Collateral Cycle
detail.abstract: Cross-country disparities in collateral technologies alone can account for large capital flows among mature economies, and allow the most advanced country to run a permanent trade deficit. When the collateral technology advantage is in creating negative beta (super safe) financial assets backed by positive beta assets, a Global Collateral Cycle emerges, with pro-cyclical gross and net flows and increased global asset price volatility. The supply of super safe assets is necessarily curtailed in downturns, providing a complementary (supply) channel to the flight to safety (demand) channel for explaining why US safe asset prices rise during crises.

title: The Underwriter's Exhibit: Employment Practices Insurance, Algorithmic Hiring, and the Disability Plaintiff's Proof

detail.title: The Underwriter's Exhibit: Employment Practices Insurance, Algorithmic Hiring, and the Disability Plaintiff's Proof
detail.abstract: An employer runs an automated screen across thousands of applications, a disabled applicant is rejected, and she files a charge. The governance industry has a product ready for that moment: documentation. Its promise is that a well kept record, bias testing, human review, an audit trail, lets the organization show the decision was defensible. At the same moment that market matured, the insurance market reached the opposite conclusion about the same technology, and carriers began writing artificial intelligence out of the very policies that would pay an employment discrimination judgment, including, by named endorsement, the employment practices line. This Article identifies a loop between those two markets that the scholarship has not examined. Where the employment practices insurer still offers coverage of an algorithmic hiring claim rather than excluding it outright, it conditions that coverage on the production of specific artifacts, whether bias testing was performed, whether a human reviewed the output, whether the tool was validated. Those artifacts are the same ones that establish a disability plaintiff's case and defeat the employer's defense. The bias test that unlocks the policy is the disparate impact statistic. The human review that unlocks the policy is the adopted recommendation that carries agency liability under Mobley v. Workday, and a balanced overall outcome cannot cure a specific discriminatory barrier under Connecticut v. Teal. The validation the underwriter asks after is the business necessity showing that Albemarle Paper Co. v. Moody places on the employer and that an unexplainable model cannot supply. Where an assessment is designed to infer a mental or neurological condition, its administration before a conditional offer is a completed violation the moment it runs, as Karraker v. Rent-A-Center shows for a personality inventory. The demand for the record is not even unique to insurance: a city audit-publication mandate and the civil rights recordkeeping rules point at the same file. And the deployer's apparent escape, running the audit under privilege, fails, because the two acts the insurance regime compels, disclosure to the underwriter and reliance on the controls as a defense, are the two classic waivers of any self evaluative privilege, the underlying facts are not privileged under Upjohn regardless, and courts have already declined to shield discrimination audits. The Article locates the remedy the litigation actually seeks, an injunction to change the design, outside insurability altogether, and argues that in this domain governance documentation does not transfer risk. It converts risk into a discoverable record while the coverage that would have paid is withdrawn.

title: Anticipation and Risk-taking: Disentangling the Effects of Delayed Information and Payment
affiliations: University of Exeter, University of Exeter Business School - Department of Economics and University of Exeter Business School - Department of Economics

detail.title: Anticipation and Risk-taking: Disentangling the Effects of Delayed Information and Payment
detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of delayed payments and delayed outcome information on individuals' risk-taking behavior. Using an online experiment with investment decisions, we isolate the effects of delayed monetary rewards and delayed risk resolution. Our findings indicate that delaying information about outcomes significantly increases risk-taking, while delaying payments alone has no statistically significant effect. This behavior is particularly pronounced in high-risk, high-reward scenarios, suggesting that anticipation plays a crucial role in decision-making under uncertainty. Our results challenge standard economic models of expected utility and discounting, highlighting the need for incorporating anticipation-based preferences into risk models. These insights have implications for financial decision-making, policy design, and gambling regulation.

title: When the Professor Writes the Prompt: Designing an AI Tutor for Introduction to Microeconomics in Distance Higher Education

detail.abstract: Large language models have become de facto study assistants for university students, yet their default behavior is pedagogically unguided: they provide direct answers without diagnosing prior knowledge, managing cognitive load, or fostering active learning. This article documents the design and implementation of a system prompt conceived as a new form of instructional material for an Introduction to Microeconomics course taught to law students in a distance higher education setting. Drawing on four evidence-based pedagogical principles-active learning, cognitive load management, formative feedback, and growth mindset-the prompt configures a large language model to act as a Socratic tutor aligned with the course's learning objectives, student profile, and disciplinary constraints. The design followed a backward design logic and included an iterative revision correcting a conversational flow problem detected in production. The prompt is made available as an open educational resource under CC BY, together with a companion Teaching and Learning Guide. The article argues that designing system prompts constitutes an emerging instructional design competence for university instructors, and that introductory economics courses are particularly well suited for this approach given the extensive representation of their content in models' pretrained knowledge. Implications for economics instructors seeking to integrate generative AI into their teaching are discussed. title: Decomposing the Oil Futures Curve: Expectations, Storage, and Risk

detail.title: Decomposing the Oil Futures Curve: Expectations, Storage, and Risk
detail.abstract: The oil futures curve embeds the expected spot price, a convenience yield, and risk premia that futures prices alone cannot separate. This paper identifies the split from the physical storage no-arbitrage restriction and crude inventories, calibrating a storage model to WTI and Brent over 2004-2026. Storage fundamentals-expected-spot growth and a dynamic convenience yield-explain nearly all of the log-basis variance, while the risk premia explain little of it. The demand premium is not negligible in level, however, opening a roughly constant gap between the futures price and the expected spot price. The recovered expectation predicts the realized spot price without systematic bias and co-moves with independent professional forecasts. A supply disruption moves the curve through the scarcity it implies more than through the compensation for bearing it, even at the largest disruption in the historical record, with inventory drawdowns absorbing most of the shock.

title: Medicare Eligibility at Age 65: Evidence from the PSID on Labor Supply, Retirement, and Household Financial Adjustment

detail.title: Medicare Eligibility at Age 65: Evidence from the PSID on Labor Supply, Retirement, and Household Financial Adjustment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or non-financial interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses publicly available, de-identified data from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID). No direct interaction with human participants was involved, and no personally identifiable information was accessed. The research is exempt from institutional ethics review under regulations governing secondary analysis of publicly available, de-identified data.

detail.abstract: I focus on the Medicare eligibility threshold at age 65 and its ability to reshape households' capacity to insure against medical utilization, financial strain, and labor-market adjustment, a core dimension of economic resilience late in the life cycle. The study contributes new evidence using a long-run household panel. Using PSID data from 2013 to 2023, the analysis exploits a fuzzy regression discontinuity framework and documents economically meaningful discontinuities around Medicare eligibility threshold. The first-stage estimates indicate that eligibility increases Medicare coverage by approximately 82 percentage points, confirming a strong discontinuity in insurance access at age 65. The results suggest that the most robust effects of Medicare eligibility occur through labor-market behavior rather than immediate changes in observed medical spending. Medicare eligibility reduces annual weeks worked by approximately 8.8 weeks, lowers employment by roughly 15 percentage points, and increases retirement probability by about 15 percentage points at the eligibility threshold. These patterns are consistent with reduced job-lock effects and a gradual transition from employment into retirement. Results remain robust across alternative bandwidth specifications, placebo cutoffs, donut-hole specifications, and global polynomial FRDD estimates. A supplementary propensity-score matching exercise provides additional evidence on observable differences between Medicare-covered and non-covered households, while the primary causal interpretation rests on the age-65 fuzzy regression discontinuity design. The paper contributes to the Medicare literature by jointly examining healthcare utilization, household financial adjustment, and labor-supply responses within a unified causal framework using long-run household panel data.

title: Feeding Tawantinsuyu: A Linear-Programming Estimate of the Inca Population before the Spanish Conquest

detail.title: Feeding Tawantinsuyu: A Linear-Programming Estimate of the Inca Population before the Spanish Conquest
detail.abstract: Estimates of the population of the Inca Empire on the eve of the Spanish conquest range from roughly four to more than thirty million, a disagreement of fourfold or greater that conditions everything we infer about the demographic catastrophe of the sixteenth century. Existing figures rest on back-projection from colonial counts, multipliers applied to tribute lists, or local settlement surveys; none derive an independent ceiling from the empire's capacity to feed itself. This paper develops such an estimate. We treat the Inca economy as a near-autarkic, labor-dominated agrarian system and pose the question as a linear program: given cultivable land by ecological zone and water regime, and pre-Hispanic crop yields, what is the largest population the food supply could sustain? The program is solved in two modes: an unconstrained, calorie-maximizing ceiling and a realistic, tuber-dominant diet, across land and yield scenarios, with parameter uncertainty propagated via Monte Carlo simulation. The food estimate is then coupled with a stable-population (Leslie-matrix) model calibrated to highland-Peru vital rates, both to verify demographic consistency and to test land-labor feasibility. The food-feasible population is near 6.9 million (90 percent interval: 5.9 to 8.0 million); even the calorie-maximizing upper bound rarely exceeds 9 million. Counts of twelve million or more are infeasible under any plausible parameterization. The realized population was growing demographically, remaining at or below this ceiling, implying that the post-conquest decline began from approximately seven, not twelve to twenty, million.

title: The Flutie Effect Revisited: Athletic Success, Postseason Milestones, and University Enrollment
affiliations: Texas Tech University, Texas Tech University and Texas Tech University

detail.title: The Flutie Effect Revisited: Athletic Success, Postseason Milestones, and University Enrollment
detail.abstract: Does college athletic success generate measurable spillovers to university academic outcomes? Using two decades of panel data on 128 FBS football programs and 246 NCAA Division I basketball programs (2004-2024), we recast the Flutie Effect as a visibility-threshold phenomenon: the academic return attaches to discrete, nationally visible postseason milestones, not to winning as such. A one-standard-deviation gain in win percentage moves applications by roughly one percent, but reaching a major bowl raises applications by 3.6 percent at their two-year peak and first-time enrollment by 2.4 percent, with cumulative applications effects of 5.4 and 7.1 percent over two and three years. College Football Playoff appearances point to larger effects still, though we treat them as suggestive. In basketball, NCAA Tournament participation-March Madness-produces its cleanest response among private institutions, where applications rise about 4.2 percent with pre-trends that pass; the full-panel enrollment response is marginal, and the larger non-FBS effect is confounded by anticipatory program build-up. The mechanism is demand expansion: applications, admissions, and enrollment scale up together while selectivity, yield, and the academic and socioeconomic composition of the entering class remain unchanged. We estimate every headline with both two-way fixed effects and a heterogeneity-robust estimator, which return very similar point estimates, and confront the power cost of sparse treatments with randomization inference, leaveone-out perturbations, and nine treatment definitions. Properly identified, the Flutie Effect is modest but real, and it expands demand precisely where national attention discontinuously rises.

title: The Confucian Fertility Paradox: Education Competition and Ultra-Low Fertility in East Asia
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - Department of Economics and Princeton University

detail.title: The Confucian Fertility Paradox: Education Competition and Ultra-Low Fertility in East Asia
detail.abstract:
Total fertility rates in East Asia have fallen to levels without historical precedent, even though the region’s Confucian heritage long placed extraordinary emphasis on family continuity and large families. We argue that this “Confucian Fertility Paradox” dissolves once we separate two strands of the tradition and recognize that modernization affected them very differently. The pro-natal strand, built on lineage continuity, ancestor worship, and reliance on sons for old-age support, was gradually switched off as child mortality fell, incomes rose, women entered the labor force, and state pensions replaced the family as the main source of security in old age. What survived was the second strand: the veneration of education and of status won through examination success, rooted in the imperial examination tradition. Under modern conditions this surviving strand reverses sign with respect to its effect on fertility. Where the historical examination system rewarded having many sons so that one might succeed, the modern single-ranking tournament rewards concentrating resources on one or two intensively educated children, and the quantity–quality tradeoff turns a once pro-natal culture into a powerful engine of low fertility. Drawing on recent empirical evidence from China and Korea, we show how education competition becomes the channel through which traditional values now suppress childbearing. We explain why standard pro-natalist policies, such as removing birth restrictions or offering cash subsidies, accomplish little when the underlying problem is a competitive equilibrium in parental investment, and we argue that policies aimed at the source of the distortion, such as structural reform of educational pathways, hold more promise.

title: Beyond a Single Metric: A Hybrid Biographical-Macrofiscal Framework for Evaluating Ghana's Finance Ministers from 1992-2024
affiliations: University of Cape Coast and

detail.title: Beyond a Single Metric: A Hybrid Biographical-Macrofiscal Framework for Evaluating Ghana's Finance Ministers from 1992-2024

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study as it did not involve human participants or animals.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding.

detail.abstract: The evaluation of finance ministers has moved, over the past century, from narrative judgments grounded in biography and reputation toward quantitative assessments built on macroeconomic and fiscal indicators. This article extends that transition to Ghana's Fourth Republic (1992-2024), proposing a hybrid political economy framework that combines ministerial biography with tenure-average macro-fiscal performance. Building on the comparative logic of Moore and Considine (2024), we construct three Ghana-specific analytical instruments: an evaluative schema spanning growth, price stability, exchange-rate stability, fiscal balance, and debt sustainability; a set of Spearman rank correlations across composite performance dimensions; and a minister-by-minister comparative profile linking biography to outcomes. The results show that performance is highly metric-dependent. Kwadwo Baah-Wiredu and Yaw Osafo-Maafo perform comparatively well on stabilization and fiscal consolidation, Kwabena Duffuor records the strongest average growth, and no minister dominates across all dimensions. Composite-dimension correlations are moderate for growth and stability (ρ = 0.643) but weak for growth and fiscal discipline (ρ = 0.357), and these relationships weaken further under a median-based robustness check for the fiscal-discipline dimension. We conclude that ministerial evaluation in Ghana and plausibly in comparable developing-country settings is best approached as inherently plural: biography provides interpretive context, but its explanatory power is conditioned by inherited macroeconomic circumstances, evolving fiscal-institutional constraints, and exogenous shocks.

title: Personal Holding Companies, Tax Progressivity, and Inequality
affiliations: University of Texas at Austin - Department of Finance, Stockholm University and University of California, Berkeley - Department of Economics

detail.title: Personal Holding Companies, Tax Progressivity, and Inequality
detail.abstract:
Tax avoidance through personal holding companies has long been viewed as a key challenge for progressive income taxation. We exploit twenty years of administrative micro-data linking firms to owners in Sweden and Norway to analyze how the use of personal holding companies varies across the income distribution and to quantify its implications in a quasi-experimental setting. About half of the income of the top 0.1% is retained in personal holding companies defined, as in US tax law, as firms for which five or fewer owners own more than 50% of the stock and that derive more than 60% of income from investment income. Event studies of shocks to operational firms’ value-added show that holding companies shield around half of dividend distributions from individual income taxation. Profits tend to remain in holding companies for long periods of time, with cumulative payout rates of 15%–20% over two decades for the highest income groups. Wealth taxes do not provide an effective backstop due to the low valuation (or exemption) of shares in private businesses. As a result, effective tax rates, all taxes included, fall from about 50% for the upper middle class to about 15%–20% among the highest-net-worth individuals. Accounting for income in holding companies erases half of the difference in the 1980–2020 rise of the top 1% fiscal income share between Nordic countries and the United States, where rules penalizing the use of holding companies have been in place since the 1930s.

title: The Scientific Return of Biodiversity Conservation: Evidence from Fishing Bans Along the Yangtze River
affiliations: Shenzhen University, , Renmin University of China, Cornell University - SC Johnson College of Business and Renmin University of China - School of Finance

detail.title: The Scientific Return of Biodiversity Conservation: Evidence from Fishing Bans Along the Yangtze River
detail.abstract:
We document arguably unintended returns of biodiversity conservation to science discovery, exploiting the 2002 fishing ban in China—an ecosystem restoration policy without explicit science-related objectives, which allows us to implement a difference-in-differences design across fish species. We find that the ban substantially increased research on affected species: funded programs rose by 21.5%, total funding by 22.8%, publications per program by 97.0%, and citations per paper by 106.7%. The effect is concentrated among researchers with geographic access to the river, and is stronger for non-extinct species and non-farmed fish species, suggesting that conservation expanded the supply of biological materials available for research. The ban also increased related public influence and patents. These results reveal that biodiversity conservation generates a significant scientific dividend through the restoration of natural research inputs, with implications for evaluating the broader benefits of ecosystem protections in an underdiscussed dimension for the science of science.

title: Central banks, debt managers, and specialness in the Bund repo market
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB) - Directorate General Research, , , German Finance Agency, Deutsche Bundesbank, European Central Bank (ECB) and Deutsche Finanzagentur

detail.title: Central banks, debt managers, and specialness in the Bund repo market
detail.abstract: Elevated repo rate specialness for German government bonds in 2016–17, and particularly in 2022-23, has often been linked to the absorption of these securities by the ECB’s asset purchase programmes. We provide the first evidence on how the debt management office mitigates these effects by jointly analyzing daily secondary-market trades and repo operations of the Deutsche Finanzagentur (DFA) alongside Eurosystem transactions in Bunds from 2015–2024. We find two points: first, that Eurosystem purchases depress repo rates about four times more than DFA purchases (0.4 bp vs 0.1 bp per 1% of free float), while DFA repo lending raises repo rates by roughly 0.2 bp per 1% of outstanding volume. Our evidence suggests that DFA interventions helped mitigate scarcity-induced specialness. Second, with elevated hedge fund demand for bonds, the overall alleviating impact was constrained by segmentation in the repo market and by the design of the facilities themselves, which aimed to prevent collateral shortages and fails-to-deliver rather than to provide price support.

title: The effects of a large energy price shock on bank credit
affiliations: and National Bank of Denmark - Research Department

detail.title: The effects of a large energy price shock on bank credit
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of the large shock to energy prices following the Russian invasion of Ukraine on bank credit to firms. To isolate the causal effect of the shock, it compares bank lending to high-energy-intensive firms to that of similar low-energy-intensive firms. Following the shock, bank credit to high-energy-intensive firms persistently declined, while their interest rates on new loans rose and other loan terms tightened. Across the distribution, safer firms reduced outstanding credit lines and paid unchanged interest rates on new bank loans, while riskier firms borrowed at higher interest rates.

title: Does Progressivity Raise Tax Capacity? Experimental Evidence from the D.R. Congo
affiliations: University of California, Davis, University College London, Harvard University, London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE), University of California, Berkeley and The World Bank

detail.title: Does Progressivity Raise Tax Capacity? Experimental Evidence from the D.R. Congo
detail.abstract:
Progressive taxation is central to high-income countries' tax systems, but developing countries typically rely on less progressive instruments. We study the introduction of progressive property taxation in a large Congolese city through a citywide field experiment conducted in partnership with the provincial government. Neighborhoods were randomly assigned to a progressive or a proportional schedule. The progressive schedule increased revenue by 56% relative to the proportional one. Gains occurred throughout the property value distribution: at the top, higher statutory rates mechanically raised revenue despite modest compliance losses; at the bottom, lower rates induced compliance gains large enough to offset lower liabilities. Cross-randomized information treatments show that taxpayers responded primarily to their own rates, not to others' rates or to the perceived fairness of the overall schedule. Effective tax rates – taxes paid as a share of property value – declined with property value and were most regressive under the progressive schedule. However, after a progressive schedule was scaled up citywide in subsequent years, targeted enforcement among high-value properties reversed this pattern, aligning statutory and effective rates. Together, the results suggest that progressive property taxation can raise fiscal capacity in low-income settings and, when paired with targeted enforcement, further shift the tax burden onto wealthier property owners.

title: The Witnessing Self and the Measure of Suffering
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Witnessing Self and the Measure of Suffering
detail.abstract: This paper reads Hyvärinen's computational theory of suffering through the Advaita Vedānta of Swami Vivekananda. For Hyvärinen, mental suffering is error signalling in a bounded reinforcement learner: frustration is reward-prediction error, threat is anticipated error, and equanimity comes from deflating expectations, a prescription that recovers Buddhist and Stoic practice. Vivekananda locates misery in desire and in non-discrimination between the real and the unreal, while the witnessing Self, the ātman, is ever-blissful and never suffers. The two accounts share a mechanism and part at the self, a division the paper states in measure-theoretic terms. Three theses follow. First, avidyā and reward-prediction error are one epistemic discrepancy: suffering is a large-deviation rate, the relative entropy of the expected world against the realized one, and reducing desire flattens it. Second, the witnessing self is the reference structure, the reference measure and invariant σ-field, not a latent state, and so lies outside the probability triple on which suffering is defined. Third, ānanda is unconditioned, a property of the reference rather than a reward, and cannot be optimized to zero. Memory enters as a measure over past paths and trauma as its concentration. The one question the mathematics cannot settle is whether the reference is a self bearing a felt tone.

title: The Fiscal Anatomy of Hyperination From the Printing Press to the Budget Constraint
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: The Fiscal Anatomy of Hyperination From the Printing Press to the Budget Constraint

keywords: scal theory of the price level

detail.abstract: Hyperinflation is conventionally defined, following Cagan (1956), as a monthly inflation rate exceeding fifty percent. This paper has three aims. First, it explains the physical mechanism by which at currency is produced and why that mechanism degrades under extreme inaction, from full multi-stage security printing to crude single-sided overprinting. Second, it develops the monetary economics that connects the press to the price level, namely the Cagan money demand function, the seigniorage or inflation-tax  curve, and the expectational instability that turns high inaction into hyperinflation. Third, it places the Hungarian collapse of 1945-1946, the most severe episode ever recorded, alongside ve comparison cases: Germany (1923), Greece (1941-1944), Nationalist China (1947-1949), Yugoslavia (1992-1994), and Zimbabwe (2007-2008). Two of these, Greece and China, are near-contemporaries of Hungary and show that the late-1940s wave of monetary collapse was a general feature of war-shattered scal states rather than a Hungarian peculiarity. The common structure is  deficits that cannot be taxed or borrowed are monetized, money demand collapses through a self-reinforcing ight from cash, and the episode ends only when the scale regime behind the printing press is credibly reformed. The printing press is the transmission mechanism, not the cause.

title: Can Mass Schooling Open Elite Education? Evidence from Nineteenth-Century Norway
affiliations: Technical University of Dortmund, University of Southern Denmark, University of Oslo and University of Southern Denmark - Department of Business and Economics

detail.title: Can Mass Schooling Open Elite Education? Evidence from Nineteenth-Century Norway
detail.abstract: We study whether Norway's 1827 rural school act broadened access to elite education. Using the universe of candidates for the Norwegian university entrance examination "examen artium" 1815-1860, we construct a candidate-level dataset of all 3,006 candidates, including birthplace and father’s occupation. After plausibly exposed cohorts entered the sample, candidates became more rural: the countryside share rose from about 45 to 52 percent and mean distance to a city from 18.0 to 21.6 km. Social opening was weaker. Farmers' sons increased from a low base but remained sharply underrepresented. The reform widened geography more than class.

title: Electrification and Development under Central Planning: Evidence from the Soviet Periphery
affiliations: Free University of Berlin

detail.title: Electrification and Development under Central Planning: Evidence from the Soviet Periphery
detail.abstract: I examine whether electricity expansion under Soviet central planning translated into broader development in the Soviet republics of Central Asia and the Caucasus from 1956-1985 and 1987-1990. The analysis focuses on education provision, organized-sector employment, and hospital infrastructure. To address endogeneity concerns, I use a historical Bartik-style instrument based on each republic's 1930 share in all-Union power-plant gross output interacted with all-Union electricity growth. The main estimates suggest that higher electricity production was not accompanied by proportional expansion in education institutions or organized-sector employment. Hospital-infrastructure results are weaker and less stable across specifications. The heterogeneity results indicate that the relationship between electricity production and organized-sector employment varied with inherited imperial backwardness and regional context. Education shows a similar but less robust pattern, while hospital infrastructure does not. These findings suggest that infrastructure did not produce uniform development effects under Soviet central planning. Its consequences depended on planning priorities and on the inherited regional conditions through which electricity expansion was absorbed.

title: Gold Extraction Potential of Aerated Glycine Solution on Paracale, Camarines Norte, and Runruno, Nueva Vizcaya Gold Ores: A Preliminary Laboratory Investigation Using the Taguchi L4 Orthogonal Array
affiliations: , Adamson University, Adamson University and Adamson University

detail.title: Gold Extraction Potential of Aerated Glycine Solution on Paracale, Camarines Norte, and Runruno, Nueva Vizcaya Gold Ores: A Preliminary Laboratory Investigation Using the Taguchi L4 Orthogonal Array

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. Ore samples utilized in this study were independently sourced from FCF Minerals and MGB Metallurgical Department, but these entities had no role in the study design, data collection and analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by Apex Mining Co. Inc. Under their SDMP DMTG

detail.abstract: The high toxicity and strict environmental regulation of sodium cyanide (NaCN) necessitate the development of safer chemical alternatives for the Philippine gold mining sector. This laboratory investigation evaluated the gold extraction potential of an environmentally benign, alkaline aerated glycine (NH2CH2COOH) leaching system on Philippine gold ores from the Runruno Gold-Molybdenum Project (Nueva Vizcaya) and the Paracale gold district (Camarines Norte). A Taguchi L4 orthogonal array executed in triplicate across 12 independent experiments screened three factors at two levels each: ore type (oxide vs. sulfide), glycine concentration (1 M vs. 2 M), and aeration duration (2 h vs. 4 h). Leaching was performed via a 24-hour Carbon-in-Leach (CIL) bottle-roll setup at ambient temperature (25 °C) and pH 10.5, with gold recovery quantified by solid-phase material balance using certified fire assay data for loaded carbon and tailings. Gold recovery plateaued at approximately 35% across all runs, with the highest recovery (35.28%) obtained using oxide ore, 1 M glycine, and 2 hours of aeration. Analysis of variance identified glycine concentration as the dominant factor (56.88% contribution), followed by aeration duration (37.99%), while ore type was statistically negligible (5.12%). The recovery ceiling is attributed to an "oxidant starvation" phenomenon: sealing the reaction vessels after the initial aeration window terminated the leaching kinetics once the dissolved oxygen was consumed, while the higher viscosity of the 2 M glycine solution further hindered oxygen mass transfer to gold particle surfaces. These findings establish a successful chemical proof-of-concept for cyanide-free leaching of complex Philippine ores and indicate that the primary process bottleneck is physical rather than chemical, with future pilot-scale work needing to prioritize continuous oxygen sparging.

title: AI-Assisted Software Engineering as Hostage Negotiation Adjusting Perspective and Strategy in Human-Agent Communication

detail.title: AI-Assisted Software Engineering as Hostage Negotiation Adjusting Perspective and Strategy in Human-Agent Communication
detail.abstract: Supervising an autonomous coding agent can feel less like programming and more like a hostage negotiation. Something you value, your codebase, is in the hands of a party that acts on it directly, while you can only influence how it acts. This paper takes that feeling seriously, as a structural allegory and not a claim about machine intent: the agent is not malicious and wants nothing. What the allegory captures is the shape of the work. A hostage negotiator does not command the other side; the craft is to build a working relationship with an unpredictable party and, through it, bring the hostage out intact. The engineer's task has the same shape. Set terms the agent will hold, read what it does against what it says, calibrate trust turn by turn, and steer a volatile collaboration toward a result you can live with. Naming that shape explains a frustration that prompt engineering and context engineering leave untouched, and it points to a skill the field has not yet named, a relational discipline and a demanding one: getting good work out of a capable, unreliable collaborator that has nothing to lose and whose hands are on something you cannot replace.

title: Beliefs in Financial Dialogue

detail.title: Beliefs in Financial Dialogue
detail.abstract: Agents' beliefs are central in macro-finance, but existing data observe them only partially. This paper turns more than 40,000 hours of financial-TV dialogue from 2012 to 2026 into speaker- and topic-resolved Q&As, providing high-frequency, cross-sectional observations on sentiment, uncertainty, and dispersion in expressed beliefs. TV-based uncertainty measures display greater topic specificity than their newspaper counterparts, co-move more closely with matched market benchmarks, and expand topic coverage. Using LLMs, we score forward-looking statements along two dimensions: direction and expressed self-uncertainty. The resulting topic-specific disagreement measures align systematically with disagreement-based benchmarks, but their relation with other uncertainty benchmarks is topic- and period-specific. The paper then studies disagreement in predictions about the future policy rate. Controlling for differences in macro projections, a mismatch in speakers' interpretations of the Fed's priorities is associated with a roughly six percentage point higher probability of a large rate-path disagreement, on par with a one-standard-deviation increase in inflation-projection disagreement. The result does not weaken when restricting the comparison to explicit conditional Fed statements and survives a battery of robustness tests. TV discourse is also rich in mental-state attributions. Fed-attribution language shows a tighter relation with market-based rate-uncertainty measures than both our own text-based uncertainty measure and standard text-based alternatives.

title: Who Benefits from Adult Education and Training? Social Stratification and Labour Market Institutions as Drivers of Unequal Returns
affiliations: and University of Lausanne - Swiss Graduate School of Public Administration

detail.title: Who Benefits from Adult Education and Training? Social Stratification and Labour Market Institutions as Drivers of Unequal Returns

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This paper is based on research carried out in the context of the Leading house GOVPET, financed by the Swiss state secretariat for education, research and innovation (SERI). Earlier versions of this paper were presented at the ESPAnet Annual Conference, Milan, 29-31 August 2025; LIVES thematic workshop, 5-6 November 2025; Joint Doctoral School Bamberg, 13-14 November 2025; and greatly benefitted from the comments we received. In addition, we would like to thank Martin Ehlert, Daniel Oesch, and Milan Thies for helpful suggestions and help with data analysis.
declarations.funderStatement: Swiss state secretariat for education, research and innovation (SERI)

detail.abstract: Adult education and training (AET) has recently gained prominence both in academic and policy debates. However, we still have an incomplete understanding how its benefits are distributed. In this article we focus on the distribution of returns to AET, and rely on Matthew effect and occupational labour market (OLM) theories. We argue that two important determinants of wage and employment returns to AET are position in social stratification and position in labour market institutional arrangements. Empirically, we focus on three countries: the UK, Germany, and Switzerland. We find no evidence of Matthew effects, but limited evidence for the opposite effect. Labour market institutions are found to play a key role, with the OLM set up being associated with stronger wage effects and its absence with positive employment effects. Overall, our analyses contribute to understanding and clarifying the complex patterns of returns to AET found in previous research.

title: Whom Should a Platform Amplify? Truth, Engagement, and Networked Polarization *
affiliations: Universite du Luxembourg - Luxembourg School of Finance

detail.title: Whom Should a Platform Amplify? Truth, Engagement, and Networked Polarization *
detail.abstract: Social-media platforms allocate reach, deciding whose content becomes widely visible. We study this as feed/reference design in a networked coordination game where users track an unknown state, coordinate with others, and hold biased ideal actions. Amplification changes both who receives information and who becomes a salient coordination reference. Making a private signal commonly observed adds a second common signal and removes the usual non-monotonicity of truth-tracking accuracy in public-signal precision; under a broadcast budget, accuracy depends only on total amplified precision. For any finite network and biases, a network intervention's effect on accuracy splits exactly into an information gain and a quadratic bias cost governed by a Katz-Bonacich influence-overlap matrix, yielding an exact source-ranking rule and a closedform amplification threshold. A reduced-form engagement objective instead favors validating, same-type links, producing more segregated networks and lower accuracy. Amplification's value depends jointly on information, bias propagation, and the platform's objective.

title: Digital Tax Administration and SME Compliance in Northern Nigeria: Evidence From Kaduna State
affiliations: , Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria and Kaduna Polytechnic

detail.title: Digital Tax Administration and SME Compliance in Northern Nigeria: Evidence From Kaduna State
detail.abstract: Despite extensive investment in e-tax platforms across Sub-Saharan Africa, empirical evidence on whether digital tax administration (DTA) translates into Nigeria remains limited and inconclusive. This study examined the effect of DTA on SME tax compliance in Kaduna State, Nigeria, with perceived trust in tax authorities, digital literacy, and internet accessibility as additional predictors. Anchored on the Technology Acceptance Model and Fiscal Exchange Theory, a quantitative cross-sectional design was adopted. Survey data were collected from 390 formally registered SMEs across five commercial local government areas using a multistage sampling procedure. Ordered logistic regression, average marginal effects, and mediation analysis were employed for statistical estimation. Findings reveal that DTA exerts no statistically significant direct effect on compliance (β = 0.030, p = .864), whereas perceived institutional trust emerges as the sole robust predictor-a one-unit increase in trust raises the probability of high compliance by approximately 7.1 percentage points (OR = 1.382, p = .047). Digital literacy registers a counter-intuitive negative association with compliance, while internet accessibility and firm size are non-significant. Mediation analysis indicates that DTA does not significantly build trust in this context, undermining the hypothesized indirect pathway to compliance. These results challenge the prevailing assumption that technology-driven fiscal reforms automatically improve voluntary compliance in infrastructure-constrained environments. The study recommends that digital tax reforms be embedded within broader institutional trust-building strategies, hybrid offline compliance pathways, and sectordifferentiated outreach programs to achieve sustainable revenue mobilization in Northern Nigeria.

reference: Virginia Public Law and Legal Theory Research Paper No. 2026-44 ; Virginia Law and Economics Research Paper No. 2026-14
title: Contract Artifacts
affiliations: Columbia University - Law School, New York University School of Law, University of Virginia School of Law and

detail.title: Contract Artifacts

publicationDetails.detailsText: Virginia Public Law and Legal Theory Research Paper No. 2026-44
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Virginia Public Law & Legal Theory Research Paper Series

publicationDetails.detailsText: Virginia Law and Economics Research Paper No. 2026-14
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Virginia Law & Economics Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: In 2020, Serta Simmons and a bare majority of its lenders exploited long-dormant provisions in a standard leveraged loan agreement to subordinate the remaining creditors. The maneuver was decried as "creditor-on-creditor violence" and ultimately rejected by the Fifth Circuit. Contract theory tells us what should have happened next. In a sophisticated, multi-trillion-dollar market, so costly a flaw should have been swiftly repaired. It was not. The standard form was patched at the surface, and the language that made Serta possible remains in place. This Article explains why. Markets, we argue, police standardized contracts only at the surface, the layer practitioners call "what is market", while language at deeper levels of the documentation drifts unattended. We call such instruments contract artifacts. That is, contracts whose surface has hardened into apparent fixity while mistakes, obsolete provisions, and subversive accretions accumulate below the market's ceiling of attention. Drawing on interviews with more than fifty practitioners, we apply the theory to the leveraged loan market and the rise of liability management transactions. The groundwork for the next Serta is already in the standard form.

title: Regime-Dependent Contagion in DeFi Liquidations: Disentangling Self-Excitation from Common Price Shocks
affiliations: Adani International School

detail.title: Regime-Dependent Contagion in DeFi Liquidations: Disentangling Self-Excitation from Common Price Shocks
detail.abstract: Liquidation events in decentralized lending protocols cluster sharply in time, but clustering alone cannot distinguish endogenous contagion from common exposure to shared price shocks. Using 18,408 ETH-collateralized liquidations on Aave V3 (January 2023-June 2026), I model hourly event counts as a negative-binomial self-exciting count process with a pricedriven background intensity and a regime-dependent excitation term. Three findings emerge. First, a naive Hawkes model with no price control is estimated to be supercritical (ν = 1.18), a known artifact of unmodeled background nonstationarity. Second, once the common price shock is controlled for, normal-regime contagion is subcritical: because the contemporaneous control over-corrects (absorbing genuine feedback) while a lagged control under-corrects (missing same-hour shocks), the two specifications bracket the normal-regime branching ratio in [0.69, 0.79]. Third, contagion is significantly regime-dependent (likelihood-ratio p < 10-5): during stress episodes, defined ex ante by trailing 24-hour ETH drawdowns exceeding 7%, the bracketed point estimates rise to [1.12, 1.81], at or above the supercritical boundary. Unconditional risk measures therefore misstate average contagion and, more importantly, understate systemic instability precisely in the episodes where cascades are most likely.

title: Tilting the Playing Field: Tax Preferences for Cooperatives and Government-Owned Enterprises
affiliations: George Mason University - Mercatus Center

detail.title: Tilting the Playing Field: Tax Preferences for Cooperatives and Government-Owned Enterprises
detail.abstract: The United States tax code does not apply evenly across all types of business activity. While private corporations are subject to corporate income tax and, in many cases, double taxation of earnings, other large segments of the economy operate under special rules or enjoy complete exemptions. Cooperatives, state and local government enterprises, and federally owned corporations together account for at least $1.4 trillion in annual commercial revenue, yet much of that activity escapes entity-level taxation. The result is a sprawling "untaxed" sector that competes directly with taxpaying firms but benefits from structural preferences written into the law. These exemptions are not minor carveouts. In the cooperative category, credit unions hold trillions in assets and compete head-to-head with banks. State and local governments operate major commercial enterprises ranging from utilities and hospitals to liquor monopolies. At the federal level, government-owned corporations such as the US Postal Service, Amtrak, and power marketing administrations generate revenues on par with large private companies. In each case, these entities function in markets where private alternatives exist, but they are governed by rules that insulate them from the tax burdens faced by ordinary businesses. Table 1 summarizes each of these three enterprise types by tax treatment, with examples and implications for tax competition. Recent analysis by tax policy expert Scott Hodge underscores the broader reach of this phenomenon. 1 Hodge finds that nonprofit organizations collectively earn more than $2.8 trillion in business-related income each year, nearly all untaxed. That includes more than $1 trillion from nonprofit hospitals alone, as well as billions in revenues from universities, insurers, sports leagues, and professional associations. By his estimates, exempting this income represents roughly $51 billion in forgone federal revenue annually. While these figures highlight that the untaxed business sector includes large swaths of nonprofit activity that compete directly with for-profit firms, little analysis has been done on the scale of state, local government, and cooperative enterprises.

title:
Concentrated Where it Matters
The Regime-Dependence of Market Power in the Spanish Day-ahead Electricity Market (2019–2024)

detail.title:
Concentrated Where it Matters
The Regime-Dependence of Market Power in the Spanish Day-ahead Electricity Market (2019–2024)
detail.abstract: We separate two questions usually conflated in electricity-market policy: where concentration lives, and whether it is exercised. On Spanish day-ahead data (2019-2024) concentration sits exactly where the price is formed: moderate on cleared energy (HHI 1,406; top-three 53%) but a deep oligopoly on the flexible, marginal-capable fleet (HHI ≈2,562; top-three 80%), a level an independent firm-capacity (ELCC) lens reproduces (2,380; 81%). Whether that structure is exercised we test against a computed competitive benchmark. Three candidate signals each appear and each dissolves under a pre-committed test: a French-outage instrument (+8.3 e/MWh) is cross-border coupling, not conduct; a broad forced-outage wedge (+50) is endogenous withholding; a tech-level wedge is benchmark convexity. The surviving signal concentrates in the high-stress regime, with a zero in slack-the signature of state-contingency: power can be exercised only when a firm is pivotal, so a slack-hour null is a null where power cannot appear. Holding net load fixed and varying pivotality through exogenous nuclear outages, the markup scales with pivotality and steepens with tightness (+33 to +57 e/MWh; day-clustered; net of a conservative benchmark). Unit-level bid curves corroborate the mechanism: the three firm-capacity owners withhold in-money capacity 2.5-3× more per hour in scarcity. We claim the gradient, not the level-cost benchmarks go blind exactly where power lives-and turn it to policy: a forward-contracting obligation lowers the markup across the entire feasible set (sign-identified), whereas a capacity mechanism's sign is not, a usable asymmetry that pins the one missing input: firm-level forward positions.

title: Two Concepts of Self-Command: Propriety, Prudence, and the Seam in the Sixth Edition of The Theory of Moral Sentiments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Two Concepts of Self-Command: Propriety, Prudence, and the Seam in the Sixth Edition of The Theory of Moral Sentiments
detail.abstract: Self-command is the hinge on which two influential readings of Adam Smith turn: the classic reconciliation of the Adam Smith Problem and the modern behavioural-economics appropriation of the impartial spectator as a far-sighted planner. This paper argues that the hinge has two leaves. Under one term Smith describes two distinct operations: spectatorial moderation, in which the imagined spectator lowers the passion itself to a shareable pitch; and prudential restraint, in which the passion remains intact while gratification is deferred for the sake of future ease. Smith grades these operations differently, gives them different psychological signatures, and, in the sixth edition of The Theory of Moral Sentiments, places them within a stratified moral architecture. Distinguishing tuning from fencing preserves the old reconciliation but corrects its overreach, and it disciplines the behavioural appropriation, which mistakes one strategy of self command for the whole of Smith’s moral psychology.

title: Displeasure Index: Subjective and Objective
affiliations: Jadavpur University

detail.title: Displeasure Index: Subjective and Objective
detail.abstract:
Peace is the concept of an ideal state within and among all people and the world. It is always very complex not only to measure but also to define. In the same way, happiness is an elusive and subjective concept and to some extent difficult to measure. On the contrary, it is easier to identify and measure people’s displeasure, which is manifested through their annoyance, dissatisfaction, worry, and unhappiness. An attempt has been made here to explore this aspect through measuring the displeasure index. Ideally, such a measure should be subjective, where the "truth" is deeply tied to how a person feels. But the present work is restricted to objective measures based on secondary data.
The analysis has been restricted to only four countries, as access to all databases is beyond the scope of the author. According to the present computation, it has been observed that displeasure with the health sector is maximum in India; displeasure with living standards is maximum in Germany; displeasure with data abuse is maximum in Germany; and displeasure with democracy is maximum in the United States. Another observation is that the displeasure index is minimum in India and maximum in the United States.
Measuring the displeasure index has important policy perspectives other than academic interest. It would provide any government with a reason to revise policies to reduce public displeasure to maintain democratic legitimacy, ensure successful implementation, and prevent civil backlash. When citizens are broadly dissatisfied, it would signal blind spots or inequity, and ignoring these grievances could severely disrupt societal functioning.

title: Paying for Backup Capacity, not Backup Delivery

detail.title: Paying for Backup Capacity, not Backup Delivery
detail.abstract: Peru pays selected gas- red generators a security-of-supply charge (CAPSE/CUCSS) for being able to run on diesel when the Camisea gas system fails. The charge is written on recognized dual capacity, not delivered diesel energy an insurance whose payout falls due exactly in the contingency it hedges, a natural setting for wrong-way risk, since the backup can fail through the same correlated shock it insures against. I test delivery in the one unambiguous physical interruption in the record: the 114 March 2026 de agration of the Camisea pipeline, which cut roughly 90% of gas ow for two weeks. A new COES IEOD/IDCOS extraction that assigns half-hourly unit MWh to gas or diesel shows the dual fleet delivered diesel energy equal to only about 20-25% of paid dual capacity over the event, intermittently and unevenly: the diesel-capable Ventanilla TG4 delivered zero, Santa Rosa ickered, Fenix converted with multi-day lags, and part of the paid Fenix block is a steam turbine that cannot itself burn diesel. Because the cut fell in the wet season, with hydropower absorbing most of the gas hole, δ ≈ 0.2 is a ceiling, not a oor the correlated bad state, a Camisea failure in a dry or El Niño year, remains untested. I frame two policies: ex-post derating of the charge by the realized factor versus ex-ante pay-for-performance that cuts the left tail. The regulator reached the same fork in 2016, scored availability-derating highest, and never enacted it; eight consecutive Precios-en-Barra xings (20172024) keep paying the formula it had declared defective

detail.abstract: The findings indicate that India has made considerable advancements in military space capabilities and has established a strong institutional framework for future growth. Nevertheless, challenges remain in areas such as integrated space command, satellite resilience, space situational awareness, rapid technological innovation, and international strategic competition. The study concludes that sustained investment in indigenous technology, stronger civil-military coordination, enhanced public-private partnerships, and international cooperation will be essential for strengthening India's strategic preparedness in the evolving domain of space warfare.

title: Public Debt and Economic Growth in the United States: Channels, Thresholds, and the Role of Monetary Policy Absorption
affiliations: George Mason University - Mercatus Center

detail.title: Public Debt and Economic Growth in the United States: Channels, Thresholds, and the Role of Monetary Policy Absorption
detail.abstract: Using quarterly US data from 1975 through 2025, this paper investigates whether rising public debt harms economic growth and, if so, through which channels. Much recent empirical work has found that debt does not harm growth, because a simple regression of GDP growth on debt finds no statistically significant effect. But this paper demonstrates that the null finding is misleading: It arises from two offsetting forces operating simultaneously, and from the Federal Reserve's (Fed's) balance sheet suppressing the primary transmission mechanism during the period when debt was highest. Three core findings emerge: quantitative easing (QE) episodes, which explains why the rate channel appeared inoperative precisely when debt was rising fastest. 3. The total debt-growth effect is obscured by a short-run demand offset. Debt-financed government spending contributes directly to measured GDP in the short run, generating an offsetting positive effect that nearly cancels the negative supply-side channel in total-effect regressions. Distinguishing these pathways is essential for policy analysis. These findings have direct implications for fiscal sustainability debates. The absence of a detectable total effect in simple regressions should not be interpreted as evidence that debt levels are inconsequential. The damage accumulates through the capital stock over years and is masked during periods of unconventional monetary policy. Fiscal projections and debt-sustainability analyses should separate short-run demand effects from long-run capital formation costs.

title: Credit Creation: The "Good", the "Bad" and the "Ugly"
affiliations: Monash University

detail.title: Credit Creation: The "Good", the "Bad" and the "Ugly"
detail.abstract: This paper develops a stock-flow consistent model to study the effects of three types of bank credit: credit for production, credit for consumption, and credit for asset speculation. The main findings are: (1) Credit for production (the "good") enables capital formation and the adoption of more productive technologies; (2) Credit for consumption (the "bad") diverts some real savings from capital formation to consumption, resulting in lower total output and less individual wealth; and (3) Credit for speculation (the "ugly") funds real wealth transfers that are unrelated to wealth creation. It can result in higher prices in the goods market, which harms all consumers including those who do not participate in asset speculation.
